key_insight: Long-range circuit noise fragility depends on fault-phase interference with the target Hamiltonian, not simply on how widely faults spread.
engineering_relevance: Noise-aware ansatz design should control transverse catalysts and balance coherent expressivity against gate-count exposure λ = pK.
method: Prove contrasting energy damage for equally extensive faults in Heisenberg chains.
Test noisy variational training with full-width long-range ZZ gates and selective catalyst suppression.
Anneal circuit sectors to identify trapping mechanisms and predict energy shifts from measured fragility.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an exact N/2 energy-damage ratio for equal-support faults; suppressing both catalyst types minimizes fragility and halves dephasing error, while catalyst annealing rescues every tested trapped trajectory.
watch_item: The reported results concern Heisenberg chains and specified circuit/noise settings; generalization to other Hamiltonians and hardware noise requires validation.
paper_title: Phase Interference and Transverse Catalysts Govern the Noise Fragility of Long-Range Variational Quantum Circuits
